claims.text: Controlled formation of nanometric carbide precipitates via post-casting heat treatment enhances the mechanical performance of refractory high-entropy alloys.
Controlled formation of nanometric carbide precipitates preserves the high-temperature stability of refractory high-entropy alloys.
Controlled formation of nanometric carbide precipitates preserves the irradiation stability of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The initial refractory high-entropy alloy is homogeneous and lacks significant secondary-phase precipitates.
An appropriately designed annealing treatment induces fine, dispersed carbide precipitates in the alloy matrix.
Rapid cooling after annealing maintains a nanometric precipitate distribution.
The induced nanoscale carbide precipitates form both at grain boundaries and within grain interiors.
Nanometric carbide precipitates impede dislocation movement.
Nanometric carbide precipitates impede grain-boundary sliding.
Impeded dislocation motion increases yield strength.
Impeded grain-boundary sliding increases creep resistance.
A small, stable precipitate dispersion minimizes adverse effects on thermal stability.
A small, stable precipitate dispersion minimizes adverse effects on irradiation stability.
The treated alloy will have greater yield strength than an alloy processed without the precipitation-inducing anneal.
The treated alloy will have greater creep resistance than an alloy processed without the precipitation-inducing anneal.
The treated alloy will retain irradiation resistance similar to that of the baseline alloy.
Excessive or coarse carbide precipitates can embrittle the alloy.
Extreme irradiation may destabilize or coarsen the carbide precipitates.
Irradiation-induced destabilization or coarsening of carbide precipitates may impair thermal stability.
